title: Mi familia
blurbEn: Ana introduces her family. You meet possessives, and the Spanish way of giving someone's age — which is not the English way.
body:
Mi familia es pequeña. Mi padre se llama Carlos y mi madre se llama Elena.

También tengo una hermana. Se llama Lucía y tiene doce años. Es muy simpática.

Mi padre trabaja en Madrid. Mi madre trabaja en casa.

¿Y tu familia? ¿Es grande o pequeña?
translationEn:
My family is small. My father is called Carlos and my mother is called Elena.

I also have a sister. She is called Lucía and she is twelve years old. She is very friendly.

My father works in Madrid. My mother works at home.

And your family? Is it big or small?

tu.note: No accent here. 'tu' means 'your'; 'tú' with an accent means 'you'.

phrases.note: The same pattern as 'me llamo', but about someone else.
Spanish says you *have* years rather than that you *are* a number of years old.
